cards.text: Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles by the Kebar River, gets another word from the LORD (Ezekiel 1:1-3). Just before this, God had him shave his head and beard with a sword and divide the hair into thirds, a picture of the judgment coming on Jerusalem (Ezekiel 5:1-12). Now God, who calls him son of man, tells him to turn his face toward something and prophesy against it.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel to set his face against something and prophesy against it. What is it?

cards.text: So Ezekiel has to speak to the mountains and hills, the ravines and valleys. Friend, I talk to my oven EVERY morning, and it hasn't answered me once.

cards.question: God tells the mountains of Israel, 'I am about to bring a sword against you…' What does He say He will destroy there?

cards.text: Then God keeps going. Their altars will be demolished, and their incense altars will be smashed.

cards.question: On the mountains of Israel, God says He will cast down their slain right in front of their ___.

cards.text: God says He will lay the corpses of the Israelites before their idols and scatter their bones around their altars. And He says this will reach wherever they live.

cards.question: God says the cities where the people of Israel live will be left standing.

cards.text: The cities will be laid waste and the high places demolished. The altars will be desecrated, the idols smashed and obliterated, and their works blotted out.

cards.question: When the slain fall among the people of Israel, what does God say they will come to know?

answers.text: That their army is too small

cards.text: After all that sword and smashing, God's message comes to one little word, 'Yet', and things start to shift. Friend, after years in the back of a junk drawer, I will take a 'yet' ANY day of the week.

cards.question: Right after the word 'Yet' in His message, God says some of the Israelites will escape the sword.

cards.text: God says a remnant will escape the sword, but they'll be scattered among the nations, carried off as captives.

cards.question: Far away in the nations where they've been carried captive, who will the survivors of Israel remember?

cards.text: They'll remember how He was grieved by their adulterous hearts that turned away from Him, and by their eyes that lusted after idols.

cards.question: Remembering how they grieved the LORD, the survivors will ___ themselves for the evil they have done.
God says His warning that He would bring this calamity on Israel was an empty threat.

cards.text: Next, Ezekiel gets something to do, not just something to say. After that sword haircut, this prophet is no stranger to acting it out (Ezekiel 5:1).

cards.question: Because of all the wicked abominations of the house of Israel, what does God tell Ezekiel to do?

answers.text: Clap his hands and stomp his feet
Tear his robe and sit in ashes
Lie on his side for many days

cards.text: He's also to cry out 'Alas!' over the house of Israel, who will fall by sword and famine and plague.

cards.question: In God's picture of sword, famine and plague, the one who is far off gets away safe.

cards.text: God speaks again: 'Then you will know that I am the LORD…' Their slain will lie on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, and under every green tree and leafy oak.

cards.question: The high hills and leafy oaks where the slain will lie were the places where the people had done what?

answers.text: Offered fragrant incense to their idols
Hid from the armies of their enemies
Built homes for their growing families

cards.text: Last, God says He will stretch out His hand against them and make the land a desolate waste, from the wilderness all the way to Diblah. And His message ends with 'Then they will know that I am the LORD.'
